workload: Fully-async multi-turn agentic RL on a 16A3B-class MoE model (Miles + SGLang + Megatron), 16 GPUs split 8 train / 8 rollout across two pods (master + worker). Each trajectory is a multi-turn tool-using episode in a remote sandbox; conversation history grows to >10k tokens, so per-turn latency depends on whether the previous turn's KV prefix is still cached on the engine that serves the next turn.
question: Why does rollout concurrency collapse after the launcher migration, and what restores it?

run-a.description: Pre-migration baseline (older launcher; separate generate-worker actors).

config.sandbox_setup_gate: 32 per the baseline launcher (not visible in the archived window; no semaphore-wait lines logged)

run-a.log_coverage: pod-console tail only (last 2000 master lines, ~40 min, 1292 worker lines); no in-process console capture exists for this run

run-b.description: Post-migration launcher, request routing through the miles router; 4 engines.

config.router_policy: least in-flight requests per worker; ignores the routing-key header
config.routing_key_affinity: configured (policy auto-set to 'manual', per-sample routing key sent as header) but NOT honored by the router

run-b.log_coverage: in-process console capture (start to ~14:17) + pod-console tail to job end (~14:33)

run-c.description: Same as the 4-engine miles-router run but 8 engines with TP=1.

config.router_policy: least in-flight requests per worker; ignores the routing-key header
config.routing_key_affinity: configured (policy auto-set to 'manual', per-sample routing key sent as header) but NOT honored by the router

run-c.log_coverage: in-process console capture (~2 h) + pod-console tail to job end

run-d.description: Routing fixed: miles router and session gateway disabled, sglang router with cache_aware policy. Sandbox gate unchanged.
run-d.log_coverage: pod-console tail only (last 2000 master lines, ~17:17-17:41) + 270 worker lines; the in-process console capture for this run is empty

notes: In-flight trajectories = max_inflight_groups x samples_per_group (32 x 8 = 256 for the post-migration runs). The sandbox setup gate is an asyncio semaphore held for sandbox create + setup + up to 3 retries; every trajectory must pass it before its first turn.
run-d is the routing-fixed reference; it still has the 64-slot sandbox gate, so its concurrency stays low for a different reason (see the sandbox task).
Labels are neutral and chronological within this task; they do not encode any external identifier.
